senses.def: caper: the pickled flower bud of the caper bush (Capparis spinosa)

etymology.text: Ultimately from Latin capparis, from Ancient Greek κάππαρις (kápparis); German Kaper came through the Romance languages (compare Italian cappero, French câpre).

pitfalls: Almost always plural: Kapern. The singular is die Kaper.

subtleties: The smaller the caper, the finer it is considered; salted capers are rinsed before use.
profile.synonymsNone: No synonym: Kapernapfel or Kapernbeere is the larger fruit of the same bush, a different product.

etymology.text: Horn (“horn”, from Old High German horn, cognate with English horn) + Gurke (“cucumber”, borrowed from Old Polish ogórek, from Byzantine Greek ἀγγούριον).

funFacts: Kiwano is a trade name from New Zealand; the plant itself comes from Africa, where it grows wild in the Kalahari.
Gurke is the same word as Greek αγγούρι (angoúri) – both from Byzantine Greek ἀγγούριον.
pitfalls: Shops say Kiwano, botanists Horngurke: both mean the same fruit.
subtleties: It is a close relative of the cucumber and the melon, and tastes mild, like cucumber with a hint of banana or lime.

short name of the plant and the gum

funFacts: German Wikipedia’s article Stängelkohl is the vegetable of Italian cime di rapa; the plant is a turnip, not a broccoli.
pitfalls: Despite the English name broccoli rabe it is no broccoli: botanically it is a form of the turnip (Brassica rapa).
subtleties: Buds, leaves and thin stems are cooked together; blanching reduces the bitterness.

homonyms.none: no other noun with this form

profile.feeling: A yellow squash whose cooked flesh falls apart into long strands, like pasta.

senses.def: spaghetti squash (Cucurbita pepo), whose cooked flesh separates into strands

examples.text: Das Fruchtfleisch vom Spaghettikürbis zerfällt in lange Fäden.
examples.tr: The flesh of the spaghetti squash falls apart into long strands.

examples.text: Spaghettikürbis mit Tomatensoße ist eine leichte Alternative zu Nudeln.
examples.tr: Spaghetti squash with tomato sauce is a light alternative to pasta.

examples.text: Den Spaghettikürbis halbiert man und backt ihn im Ofen.
examples.tr: You halve the spaghetti squash and bake it in the oven.

collocations.tr: the strands of the spaghetti squash

etymology.text: Spaghetti (borrowed from Italian spaghetti) + Kürbis (“pumpkin, squash”, from Old High German kurbiȥ).

funFacts: It is the same species as zucchini and pattypan: Cucurbita pepo.
pitfalls: Genitive and plural double the s: des Spaghettikürbisses, die Spaghettikürbisse.
subtleties: The strands only appear after cooking; you scrape them out with a fork.
profile.synonymsNone: No other common name; seed catalogues sometimes add the variety name.

homonyms.none: no other noun with this form

profile.feeling: Big yellow flowers, stuffed and fried – a summer delicacy from the garden.

senses.def: zucchini flower, courgette blossom

examples.text: Gefüllte Zucchiniblüten sind eine italienische Spezialität.
examples.tr: Stuffed zucchini flowers are an Italian speciality.

examples.text: Man erntet meistens die männlichen Zucchiniblüten.
examples.tr: Usually the male zucchini flowers are harvested.

examples.text: Zucchiniblüten sind sehr empfindlich und halten nur einen Tag.
examples.tr: Zucchini flowers are very delicate and only keep for a day.

synonyms.nuance: Swiss form, as Zucchetti is the Swiss word for zucchini

etymology.text: Zucchini (borrowed from Italian zucchini, plural of zucchino) + Blüte (“blossom”, from Old High German bluot).
etymology.src: Wiktionary (kaikki.org), for the parts Zucchini and Blüte

funFacts: Greek κολοκυθοανθοί (stuffed with rice and herbs) and Turkish kabak çiçeği dolması are the same dish idea as Italian fiori di zucca ripieni.
pitfalls: The female flowers have a little zucchini at the base; if you pick them, there will be no zucchini.
subtleties: The flowers close in the afternoon; they are picked in the morning and used the same day.

homonyms.none: no other noun with this form

profile.feeling: A tender, cone-shaped spring cabbage, milder than white cabbage.

senses.def: pointed cabbage, sweetheart cabbage (a conical form of white cabbage)

examples.text: Spitzkohl ist zarter als Weißkohl.
examples.tr: Pointed cabbage is more tender than white cabbage.

examples.text: Ich mache einen Krautsalat aus Spitzkohl.
examples.tr: I’m making a coleslaw from pointed cabbage.

examples.text: Auf den Fildern bei Stuttgart wächst das bekannte Filderkraut, ein Spitzkohl.
examples.tr: On the Filder plateau near Stuttgart grows the famous Filderkraut, a pointed cabbage.

synonyms.nuance: southern German name, as in Filderspitzkraut

etymology.text: From spitz (“pointed”) + Kohl (“cabbage”). Cognate with Danish spidskål, Dutch spitskool and Swedish spetskål.

funFacts: Filderspitzkraut from near Stuttgart is protected as an EU geographical indication.
pitfalls: Plural Spitzkohle is rare; say zwei Köpfe Spitzkohl.
subtleties: Because its leaves are thin and tender, it cooks in a few minutes and can be eaten raw.

homonyms.none: no other noun with this form

profile.feeling: Tiny yellow corncobs from a jar or a wok – crunchy and eaten whole.

senses.def: baby corn: very young ears of maize, eaten whole

examples.text: Maiskölbchen isst man mit dem Kolben.
examples.tr: Baby corn is eaten with the cob.

examples.text: Im Glas gibt es Maiskölbchen süßsauer eingelegt.
examples.tr: In jars there is sweet-and-sour pickled baby corn.

examples.text: Ich werfe ein paar Maiskölbchen in den Wok.
examples.tr: I throw a few baby corns into the wok.

synonyms.nuance: common shop name, a mass noun
shop name on packages

etymology.text: Diminutive of Maiskolben: Mais (“maize”, from Spanish maíz, from Taíno) + Kolben (“cob, club”, from Old High German kolbo) + -chen.

funFacts: Chinese 玉米笋 (yùmǐsǔn, “corn shoot”). The cobs are picked a few days after the silk appears, before the kernels develop.
pitfalls: -chen nouns are always neuter and do not change in the plural: das Maiskölbchen, die Maiskölbchen.
subtleties: Unlike ripe corn on the cob, the whole cob is eaten.

homonyms.none: no other noun with this form

profile.feeling: A dark green, ribbed squash shaped like an acorn, halved and baked.

senses.def: acorn squash (Cucurbita pepo), a small ribbed squash shaped like an acorn

examples.text: Der Eichelkürbis hat tiefe Rippen und eine dunkelgrüne Schale.
examples.tr: The acorn squash has deep ribs and a dark green skin.

examples.text: Einen Eichelkürbis halbiert man und füllt ihn.
examples.tr: You halve an acorn squash and stuff it.

examples.text: Eichelkürbisse sieht man in Deutschland selten im Supermarkt.
examples.tr: In Germany you rarely see acorn squashes in the supermarket.

synonyms.nuance: half-English name used in seed catalogues

etymology.text: Eichel (“acorn”, from Old High German eihhila, related to Eiche “oak”) + Kürbis (“pumpkin, squash”, from Old High German kurbiȥ).
etymology.src: Wiktionary (kaikki.org), for the parts Eichel and Kürbis

funFacts: Despite its winter-squash use, acorn squash is the same species as zucchini (Cucurbita pepo).
pitfalls: Eichel alone means “acorn” (in anatomy also the glans); Eichelkürbis is only the squash.
subtleties: Its skin is thin enough to eat when baked.

homonyms.none: no other noun with this form

profile.feeling: Plump, crunchy pods that are eaten whole – sweet straight from the garden.

senses.def: sugar snap pea (Pisum sativum, sugar pea group), eaten pod and all

examples.text: Zuckererbsen isst man mit der Schote.
examples.tr: Sugar snap peas are eaten with the pod.

examples.text: Die Kinder naschen die Zuckererbsen direkt im Garten.
examples.tr: The children nibble the sugar snaps right in the garden.

examples.text: Zuckererbsen nur kurz blanchieren, damit sie knackig bleiben.
examples.tr: Blanch sugar snaps only briefly so they stay crunchy.

collocations.tr: the pods of the sugar snap pea

synonyms.nuance: usually the flat snow pea, but shops use both words loosely
Swiss word for edible-pod peas

etymology.text: Zucker (“sugar”) + Erbse (“pea”, from Old High German arawīz).

funFacts: In Swiss German both snow peas and sugar snaps are Kefen.
pitfalls: Zuckererbse (round, thick pods) and Zuckerschote (flat pods, snow pea) are often mixed up, even in shops.
subtleties: Pull off the string along the seam before cooking; the whole pod is sweet.
